daily_life.definition: A regular sequence of actions followed systematically.
daily_life.advanced_definition: A customary procedure established through repeated practice.
daily_life.contextual_example: Establishing a consistent morning study routine dramatically improves vocabulary retention.

daily_life.definition: To travel regularly between one's residence and workplace.
daily_life.simple_definition: Travel back and forth to work.
daily_life.advanced_definition: To journey recurringly between home and office.
daily_life.contextual_example: Many professionals prefer working remotely to avoid a gruelling two-hour daily commute.
common_mistakes: Refers strictly to recurring transit, not holidays.

daily_life.definition: Free time when one is not working or occupied.
daily_life.advanced_definition: Time provided by the cessation of work or duties.
daily_life.contextual_example: Digital entertainment has transformed contemporary leisure pursuits among adolescents.
common_mistakes: 'Leisurely' is an adjective, not a noun.

daily_life.definition: Routine household tasks such as cleaning or cooking.
daily_life.advanced_definition: Unpleasant or tedious but necessary domestic duties.
daily_life.contextual_example: Sharing domestic chores equitably fosters marital harmony.

daily_life.definition: To perform more than one activity at the same time.
daily_life.advanced_definition: Concurrent cognitive execution of multiple tasks.
daily_life.contextual_example: Attempting to multitask while studying impairs long-term memory consolidation.

daily_life.definition: Involving much sitting and little physical exercise.
daily_life.advanced_definition: Characterized by physical inactivity and seated posture.
daily_life.contextual_example: A sedentary lifestyle significantly elevates the risk of cardiovascular disease.
daily_life.ielts_usefulness: High-scoring in health and lifestyle essays.

daily_life.definition: A short trip to deliver or collect something or accomplish a job.
daily_life.advanced_definition: A brief journey undertaken on minor business.
daily_life.contextual_example: He spent the afternoon running domestic errands across the city.

daily_life.definition: Doing something or arriving at the agreed time; on time.
daily_life.advanced_definition: Strictly observant of an appointed hour.
daily_life.contextual_example: Being punctual for professional interviews conveys organizational reliability.

education.definition: The subjects comprising an academic program of study.
education.advanced_definition: The overarching aggregate of courses provided by an institution.
education.contextual_example: Secondary curricula should emphasize empirical reasoning over rote memorization.

education.definition: The method and theoretical practice of teaching.
education.advanced_definition: The theoretical and practical methodology of instruction.
education.contextual_example: Constructivist pedagogy encourages students to discover scientific principles actively.
common_mistakes: Stress is on the first syllable.

education.definition: Relating to university or post-secondary education.
education.advanced_definition: The third stage of formalized post-school education.
education.contextual_example: Subsidizing tertiary education creates a highly skilled workforce.

education.definition: Mechanical repetition of facts to be learned without comprehension.
education.contextual_example: Rote learning is ineffective for developing critical thinking competencies.

education.definition: The ability to read and write; foundational competence.
education.advanced_definition: Foundational competence in textual or symbolic decoding.
education.contextual_example: Financial literacy is essential for young adults managing credit.

education.definition: Relating to mental processes of reasoning and perception.
education.contextual_example: Bilingual education bolsters cognitive flexibility in young learners.

education.definition: An outline of the subjects in a specific course.
education.advanced_definition: Document outlining topics and deadlines for one course.
education.contextual_example: The updated syllabus includes modules on artificial intelligence ethics.

education.definition: Relating to practical employment training and trades.
education.advanced_definition: Imparting practical career competencies for skilled trades.
education.contextual_example: Vocational apprenticeships bridge the gap between school and industry.

work_and_careers.definition: Financial compensation paid for work or services.
work_and_careers.advanced_definition: Reward or recompense for services rendered.
work_and_careers.contextual_example: Executive remuneration packages should be contingent on sustainable corporate performance.

work_and_careers.definition: A formal assessment of the performance or value of an employee.
work_and_careers.contextual_example: Annual performance appraisals provide workers with structured career feedback.

work_and_careers.definition: The state of being no longer needed; dismissal because a job ceases to exist.
work_and_careers.advanced_definition: Termination of employment resulting from workforce reduction.
work_and_careers.contextual_example: Automation in manufacturing has resulted in involuntary redundancies across the sector.
common_mistakes: In UK: 'made redundant' means laid off, not fired for misconduct.

work_and_careers.definition: A period of trial and evaluation for a new employee.
work_and_careers.advanced_definition: Testing period during which an employee's competence is vetted.
work_and_careers.contextual_example: During his six-month probationary period, his coding proficiency was closely monitored.
common_mistakes: Also used in criminal justice, but distinct in business.

work_and_careers.definition: Development or improvement; promotion in a career.
work_and_careers.advanced_definition: Upward progression within an organizational hierarchy.
work_and_careers.contextual_example: Mentorship programs significantly enhance career advancement opportunities for women.
common_mistakes: Uncountable when meaning abstract career progress.

work_and_careers.definition: Working from home using the internet, email, and telephone.
work_and_careers.advanced_definition: Remote execution of employment duties via telecommunication links.
work_and_careers.contextual_example: Telecommuting affords workers substantial autonomy while decreasing corporate overheads.

work_and_careers.definition: The ability to do something successfully or efficiently.
work_and_careers.simple_definition: Ability and skill to do a job.
work_and_careers.advanced_definition: Sufficiency of qualification, knowledge, or capacity.
work_and_careers.contextual_example: Demonstrated linguistic competence is an essential prerequisite for international diplomacy.

work_and_careers.definition: The rate at which employees leave a workforce and are replaced.
work_and_careers.simple_definition: Rate workers quit and get replaced.
work_and_careers.advanced_definition: The cycle of staff departure and replacement in an enterprise.
work_and_careers.contextual_example: Toxic management cultures inevitably lead to high staff turnover and diminished morale.
common_mistakes: Also means business financial revenue in British English.

technology.definition: Relating to an algorithm or process of computer calculation.
technology.advanced_definition: Pertaining to mathematical step-by-step computational procedures.
technology.contextual_example: Algorithmic decision-making in financial credit assessment can inadvertently perpetuate bias.

technology.definition: The use of automatic equipment in manufacturing or data processing.
technology.advanced_definition: The execution of processes by mechanical or electronic means without human intervention.
technology.contextual_example: Industrial automation increases manufacturing throughput while transforming labor demand.

technology.definition: Close observation, especially of a suspected person or public space.
technology.advanced_definition: Continuous systematic oversight of persons or territories for security purposes.
technology.contextual_example: The ubiquity of facial recognition surveillance cameras sparks intense debate over civil privacy.

technology.definition: Rapid increase in the number or amount of something.
technology.advanced_definition: Exponential growth, reproduction, or diffusion of phenomena.
technology.contextual_example: The rapid proliferation of smartphones has altered social interactions among teenagers.

technology.definition: Measures taken to protect computers and networks against unauthorized access.
technology.advanced_definition: The protection of internet-connected systems from digital attacks.
technology.contextual_example: Hospitals must fortify their cybersecurity protocols to protect sensitive patient records.
common_mistakes: Single compound word in modern English.

technology.definition: No longer produced or used; out of date.
technology.advanced_definition: No longer in use or fashion because replaced by modern innovation.
technology.contextual_example: Compact discs have become virtually obsolete with the advent of cloud music streaming.
common_mistakes: 'Planned obsolescence' is an important economic concept.

technology.definition: Innovating in a way that displaces an established technology or industry.
technology.simple_definition: Changing how an entire industry works.
technology.advanced_definition: Upending conventional market structures through radical innovation.
technology.contextual_example: Generative artificial intelligence represents a profoundly disruptive technology across creative fields.
common_mistakes: In business, 'disruptive' is highly positive, unlike in schooling.

technology.advanced_definition: Existing or being encountered simultaneously in all locations.
technology.contextual_example: Mobile computing has become so ubiquitous that digital disconnection is increasingly difficult.

science.definition: Based on, concerned with, or verifiable by observation rather than theory.
science.simple_definition: Based on real experiment and data.
science.advanced_definition: Originating in or corroborated by physical observation or experimentation.
science.contextual_example: Scientific theories require rigorous empirical verification before gaining institutional consensus.

science.definition: A proposed explanation for a phenomenon, made as a starting point for investigation.
science.advanced_definition: A provisional proposition formulated to deduce consequences testable by reality.
science.contextual_example: The astrophysicist proposed a novel hypothesis explaining cosmic radiation fluctuations.

science.definition: Deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected.
science.advanced_definition: Inconsistent with standard empirical expectations or established laws.
science.contextual_example: Researchers discarded the anomalous laboratory readings to preserve sample integrity.

science.definition: Confirm or give support to a statement, theory, or finding.
science.advanced_definition: To strengthen or substantiate with independent secondary evidence.
science.contextual_example: Independent clinical trials subsequently corroborated the efficacy of the vaccine.

science.definition: Repeat or duplicate an experiment or process to obtain a consistent result.
science.advanced_definition: To reproduce experimental conditions to ascertain validity.
science.contextual_example: Scientific integrity requires that peer laboratories be capable of replicating all published findings.
common_mistakes: 'Replication crisis' is a prominent modern topic.

science.definition: A typical example or pattern of something; a distinct scientific worldview.
science.advanced_definition: A philosophical and theoretical framework of a scientific school or discipline.
science.contextual_example: Quantum mechanics triggered a profound paradigm shift in theoretical physics.

science.definition: Made by chemical synthesis, especially to imitate a natural product.
science.advanced_definition: Formed by artificial chemical process rather than natural extraction.
science.contextual_example: Synthetic fertilizers elevated crop yields but caused subsequent riverine eutrophication.
common_mistakes: Do not confuse with 'synthesized' in literature.

science.definition: A substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without undergoing permanent change; an agent of change.
science.advanced_definition: An agency or substance that accelerates transitions without being consumed.
science.contextual_example: Government funding for public infrastructure serves as a major catalyst for regional economic growth.
common_mistakes: Widely used metaphorically in politics and economics.

environment.definition: Meeting present needs without compromising future generations.
environment.advanced_definition: Development that balances ecological, social, and economic imperatives.
environment.contextual_example: Corporate commitment to environmental sustainability is no longer optional.
environment.ielts_usefulness: Essential for all green Task 2 essays.

environment.definition: The action of reducing the severity or seriousness of something.
environment.advanced_definition: Systematic alleviation of environmental hazards or carbon output.
environment.contextual_example: Investing in tidal flood barriers is a crucial climate mitigation strategy.

environment.definition: The variety of plant and animal life in a particular habitat.
environment.advanced_definition: Ecological variety of species and genetic alleles within a biome.
environment.contextual_example: Deforestation in the Amazon basin causes catastrophic loss of biodiversity.

environment.definition: Use up the supply or resources of something.
environment.advanced_definition: To exhaust natural reservoirs, minerals, or energy supplies.
environment.contextual_example: Intensive commercial irrigation continues to deplete regional aquifers.

environment.definition: The permanent clearing of trees and forested areas by humans.
environment.advanced_definition: The large-scale clearing of forests for agricultural or timber extraction.
environment.contextual_example: Tropical deforestation is a major anthropogenic driver of atmospheric greenhouse gas accumulation.

environment.definition: A biological community of interacting organisms and their physical environment.
environment.simple_definition: Natural community of plants and animals.
environment.advanced_definition: A self-sustaining complex of plant, animal, and microorganism communities.
environment.contextual_example: Coral reefs are among the most fragile ecosystems on the planet.

environment.definition: Capable of being replenished naturally within a human lifespan.
environment.advanced_definition: Derived from inexhaustible natural sources like sun and wind.
environment.contextual_example: Nations must transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy sources.

environment.definition: Liquid waste or sewage discharged into a river or the sea.
environment.advanced_definition: Untreated chemical or municipal wastewater released into waterways.
environment.contextual_example: Triclosan and industrial effluents severely contaminate local river systems.

health.definition: Relating to the heart and blood vessels.
health.simple_definition: Related to heart and blood circulation.
health.contextual_example: Aerobic physical exertion promotes long-term cardiovascular health.

health.definition: A widespread occurrence of an infectious disease in a community.
health.advanced_definition: Outbreak of disease affecting disproportionate numbers at a particular time.
health.contextual_example: Health authorities mobilized resources to suppress the influenza epidemic.

health.definition: The action of vaccinating someone to produce immunity.
health.advanced_definition: Artificial induction of active acquired immunity through antigenic delivery.
health.contextual_example: Universal childhood inoculation eradicated smallpox globally.

health.definition: Relating to the process of providing or obtaining nourishment.
health.advanced_definition: Pertaining to the intake and biochemical assimilation of dietary nutrients.
health.contextual_example: Fast food generally lacks essential nutritional value.

health.definition: Persisting for a long time or constantly recurring.
health.advanced_definition: Designating disease or condition enduring over extensive duration.
health.contextual_example: Chronic sleep deprivation impairs cognitive performance and emotional resilience.

health.definition: Relating to the healing of disease; producing good effects on mind/body.
health.advanced_definition: Serving to cure or alleviate disease or mental distress.
health.contextual_example: Gardening and nature walks exert a therapeutic influence on anxiety.

health.definition: Long life; existence for a long duration.
health.advanced_definition: The duration of individual life beyond average cohort benchmarks.
health.contextual_example: Advances in biomedical sanitation have dramatically expanded human longevity.

health.definition: Making someone very weak and infirm.
health.simple_definition: Severely weakening the body or mind.
health.advanced_definition: Causing serious impairment of strength, vitality, or cognitive ability.
health.contextual_example: Chronic fatigue syndrome can be a debilitating condition that severely limits daily activity.
health.ielts_usefulness: High-scoring lexis for public health and illness prompts.

society.definition: The process of making an area more urban; population shift from country to city.
society.advanced_definition: Demographic transition wherein populations aggregate into urban centers.
society.contextual_example: Rapid urbanization places immense pressure on municipal sanitation and transit.

society.definition: The arrangement or classification of something into different groups or layers.
society.advanced_definition: Hierarchical societal organization structuring unequal access to resources.
society.contextual_example: Unequal access to elite education perpetuates rigid social stratification.

society.definition: The action or state of cohering or sticking together; unity in society.
society.advanced_definition: Interpersonal trust and solidarity holding communities together.
society.contextual_example: Community sports festivals strengthen local social cohesion across diverse immigrant groups.
common_mistakes: Essential criteria name in Writing (Coherence and Cohesion).

society.definition: Renovation of urban areas resulting in displacement of lower-income residents.
society.advanced_definition: Urban redevelopment attracting affluent residents and escalating property values.
society.contextual_example: While gentrification renovates historic architecture, it frequently displaces working-class families.

society.definition: Treated as insignificant or peripheral in a society.
society.simple_definition: Excluded or pushed to the edge.
society.advanced_definition: Relegated to powerless outer fringes of social, economic, or political life.
society.contextual_example: Community legal clinics provide pro bono assistance to marginalized populations.

society.simple_definition: Unfair difference in money or health.
society.advanced_definition: Incongruity or inequality in opportunity, treatment, or distribution.
society.contextual_example: The economic disparity between rural agricultural regions and coastal metropolises continues to widen.

society.definition: Statistical data relating to the population and particular groups within it.
society.advanced_definition: Quantitative characteristics of human populations such as age, gender, and income.
society.contextual_example: Shifting demographics in aging societies necessitate urgent pension system reforms.

society.definition: The basic physical and organizational structures needed for the operation of a society.
society.advanced_definition: Foundational public works enabling economic transport, energy, and communication.
society.contextual_example: Investing in green public transit infrastructure accelerates urban decarbonization.

culture.definition: Property, traditions, or culture inherited from past generations.
culture.advanced_definition: Enduring cultural legacy, traditions, and historical assets.
culture.contextual_example: UNESCO works to preserve tangible and intangible cultural heritage worldwide.

culture.definition: The process of absorbing and integrating people into a wider society or culture.
culture.advanced_definition: Sociocultural integration wherein minorities adopt customs of dominant culture.
culture.contextual_example: Language acquisition programs facilitate smooth cultural assimilation for newly arrived refugees.

culture.definition: The act of maintaining something in its original or existing state.
culture.advanced_definition: Systematic conservation to prevent decay or destruction of cultural assets.
culture.contextual_example: Historical preservation laws prevent developers from demolishing Victorian public libraries.

culture.definition: Originating or occurring naturally in a particular place; native.
culture.advanced_definition: Originating organically within a region prior to colonization.
culture.contextual_example: Indigenous knowledge regarding medicinal plants is invaluable for botanical pharmacology.

culture.definition: Traditional beliefs, customs, and stories of a community passed by word of mouth.
culture.advanced_definition: The oral narrative traditions and superstitions of a cultural group.
culture.contextual_example: Celtic folklore contains rich allegorical tales of enchanted forests and ancient heroes.

culture.definition: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty.
culture.advanced_definition: Pertaining to philosophical taste and sensory appreciation of art.
culture.contextual_example: Modernist architecture emphasizes functional utility over ornate aesthetic embellishment.

culture.definition: Great in importance, extent, or size; relating to a monument.
culture.advanced_definition: Possessing imposing scale and historical gravitas.
culture.contextual_example: The restoration of Notre-Dame Cathedral represents a monumental feat of master craftsmanship.

culture.definition: The transmission of customs or beliefs from generation to generation.
culture.advanced_definition: Inherited established pattern of thought, action, or behavior.
culture.contextual_example: Sharing a communal feast during the harvest festival is an enduring national tradition.

business.definition: A person who sets up a business, taking on financial risks in the hope of profit.
business.advanced_definition: An innovator who coordinates capital and labor to commercialize a novel venture.
business.contextual_example: Young tech entrepreneurs in Silicon Valley disrupted conventional financial banking.

business.definition: The exclusive possession or control of the supply of or trade in a commodity.
business.simple_definition: Single company controlling an entire market.
business.advanced_definition: Market structure characterized by a single supplier exerting unchecked pricing power.
business.contextual_example: Antitrust regulatory agencies monitor tech conglomerates to prevent uncompetitive monopolies.

business.definition: Income, especially when of an organization and of a substantial nature.
business.advanced_definition: Total gross financial proceeds before deducting expenses and taxation.
business.contextual_example: The corporation reported an eighteen percent surge in quarterly advertising revenue.

business.definition: A company controlled by a holding or parent company.
business.simple_definition: Branch company owned by a bigger parent.
business.advanced_definition: An enterprise whose majority voting shares are owned by another corporate entity.
business.contextual_example: The multinational automobile giant manufactures electric batteries through a specialized German subsidiary.

business.definition: The state or degree of being easily or conveniently done.
business.simple_definition: Practical possibility of doing a project.
business.advanced_definition: The practical and economic viability of an intended technical proposal.
business.contextual_example: Before breaking ground on the railway extension, civil engineers conducted a comprehensive feasibility study.

business.definition: A person with an interest or concern in something, especially a business.
business.simple_definition: Anyone affected by a company's decisions.
business.advanced_definition: Any party having a direct or indirect vested interest in organizational actions.
business.contextual_example: Corporate leadership consulted community stakeholders before expanding the industrial facility.

business.definition: The state of being unable to pay the money owed, by a person or company.
business.advanced_definition: Financial failure wherein current liabilities exceed liquid assets and cash-flow.
business.contextual_example: Escalating interest rates precipitated widespread corporate insolvencies across the retail sector.

business.definition: A number of different things or parts that are grouped together; a multi-industry corporation.
business.advanced_definition: A diversified multi-industry enterprise resulting from multiple commercial mergers.
business.contextual_example: The media conglomerate controls major newspapers, broadcasting networks, and film production studios.

travel.definition: A planned route or journey; a travel schedule.
travel.advanced_definition: A documented schedule detailing destinations, flight numbers, and accommodation.
travel.contextual_example: Our travel agent forwarded an itemized itinerary covering our seven-day tour of Kyoto.

travel.definition: The place to which someone or something is going or being sent.
travel.advanced_definition: The terminal arrival point of a journey.
travel.contextual_example: Bali has evolved into one of the most sought-after holiday destinations in Southeast Asia.

travel.definition: The friendly and generous reception and entertainment of guests; hotel industry.
travel.advanced_definition: Generous social hosting, or the commercial lodging and food services industry.
travel.contextual_example: We were deeply touched by the warm hospitality extended by the rural village elders.

travel.definition: A short journey or trip, especially one taken as a leisure activity.
travel.advanced_definition: A brief pleasure outing organized for recreational exploration.
travel.contextual_example: The cruise package includes a guided excursion to ancient archaeological ruins.

travel.definition: The carrying of people, goods, or materials from one place to another.
travel.advanced_definition: Passage or transportation from one spatial terminal to another.
travel.contextual_example: The municipality invested forty million pounds into high-speed urban transit corridors.

travel.definition: The state of being congested or overcrowded, especially traffic.
travel.advanced_definition: Severe impediment of traffic movement caused by excessive vehicular volume.
travel.contextual_example: Implementing a downtown congestion charge dramatically reduced peak-hour traffic delays.

travel.definition: Tourism directed towards exotic natural environments to support conservation.
travel.advanced_definition: Environmentally responsible travel to natural areas that conserves the ecosystem.
travel.contextual_example: Costa Rica pioneered sustainable ecotourism, financing national parks through visitor permits.

travel.definition: Provide lodging or sufficient space for; fit in with the wishes of.
travel.advanced_definition: To furnish with lodging, or adjust harmoniously to requirements.
travel.contextual_example: The newly refurbished conference hotel can accommodate up to eight hundred delegates.

government.definition: Laws, considered collectively; the process of enacting laws.
government.advanced_definition: Statutory enactments authored and ratified by a legislative body.
government.contextual_example: Parliament passed landmark environmental legislation penalizing industrial carbon emissions.
common_mistakes: Uncountable noun; do not say 'a legislation'.

government.definition: The official power to make legal decisions and judgments.
government.simple_definition: Legal authority of a court or territory.
government.advanced_definition: The territorial and constitutional authority granted to a legal agency.
government.contextual_example: Cybercrimes committed across international borders create complex jurisdiction challenges for police.

government.definition: Supreme power or authority; the authority of a state to govern itself.
government.advanced_definition: Autonomous political self-determination free from external geopolitical control.
government.contextual_example: Small island states fiercely assert their territorial sovereignty over surrounding maritime fisheries.

government.definition: A system of government in which decisions are made by state officials; complex administration.
government.advanced_definition: Administrative apparatus structured around rigid procedural rules and hierarchies.
government.contextual_example: Excessive civil bureaucracy stifles entrepreneurial innovation and delays public construction.

government.definition: A general vote by the electorate on a single political question for a direct decision.
government.simple_definition: Public vote on one big law.
government.advanced_definition: A direct constitutional mechanism submitting legislative questions to popular ballot.
government.contextual_example: The electorate voted decisively in favor of constitutional reform in the nationwide referendum.

government.definition: A member of an area who elects a representative to parliament.
government.advanced_definition: An enfranchised citizen entitled to political representation.
government.contextual_example: The member of parliament held a weekly surgery to hear grievances from local constituents.
common_mistakes: Also means an elementary component in chemistry.

government.definition: The action or manner of governing a state or organization.
government.simple_definition: Way a country or company is run.
government.advanced_definition: The strategic exercise of executive management, ethics, and regulatory oversight.
government.contextual_example: Transparent institutional governance is essential to prevent corruption in developing economies.

government.definition: A formally concluded and ratified agreement between states.
government.advanced_definition: A legally binding contractual covenant ratified between sovereign nations.
government.contextual_example: Signatories to the non-proliferation treaty agreed to permit unannounced nuclear inspections.

economics.definition: A general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.
economics.advanced_definition: A persistent macroeconomic escalation in general price indices eroding real purchasing parity.
economics.contextual_example: Surging energy tariffs triggered acute consumer price inflation across Western economies.

economics.definition: A period of temporary economic decline during which trade and industrial activity fall.
economics.advanced_definition: Consecutive quarters of negative GDP contraction accompanied by escalating unemployment.
economics.contextual_example: During the deep financial recession of 2008, thousands of mortgage borrowers defaulted.
common_mistakes: A prolonged recession is termed a 'depression'.

economics.definition: Relating to government revenue, especially taxes.
economics.simple_definition: Related to government tax and spending.
economics.advanced_definition: Pertaining to public budgetary management and government revenue collection.
economics.contextual_example: The chancellor introduced expansionary fiscal policies to stimulate consumer demand.

economics.definition: The amount by which something, especially a sum of money, is too small.
economics.advanced_definition: The excess of public expenditure over revenue receipts within a fiscal period.
economics.contextual_example: Persistent trade deficits can depreciate a sovereign currency on international foreign exchanges.

economics.definition: A tax or duty to be paid on a particular class of imports or exports.
economics.advanced_definition: A customs duty levied by governments on cross-border merchandise to shield domestic industries.
economics.contextual_example: The imposition of retaliatory steel tariffs sparked an escalating trade war between the nations.

economics.definition: A raw material or primary agricultural product that can be bought and sold.
economics.simple_definition: Raw materials like oil, wheat, gold.
economics.advanced_definition: A standardized material good traded interchangeably on global mercantile exchanges.
economics.contextual_example: Crude petroleum remains the most volatile commodity in international mercantile exchanges.

economics.definition: The availability of liquid assets to a market or company; cash on hand.
economics.advanced_definition: The ease with which an asset can be converted into ready currency without capital loss.
economics.contextual_example: Central banks injected emergency liquidity into the banking system to avert interbank contagion.
economics.ielts_usefulness: Bank runs and market crash reading.

economics.definition: Support financially; pay part of the cost of producing something.
economics.simple_definition: Give government money to help pay for.
economics.advanced_definition: To furnish financial aid from public treasury to keep price low.
economics.contextual_example: The government subsidizes public transport to encourage citizens to leave cars at home.

media.definition: The suppression or prohibition of any parts of books, news, or films considered politically unacceptable.
media.advanced_definition: Official restriction or suppression of expressive communication deemed subversive or immoral.
media.contextual_example: Authoritarian regimes deploy rigorous internet censorship to suppress political dissent.

media.definition: The activity or profession of writing for newspapers, magazines, or news websites.
media.advanced_definition: The gathering, verification, and presentation of factual news and public affairs.
media.contextual_example: Investigative journalism plays an indispensable watchdog role in democratic accountability.

media.definition: False or inaccurate information, especially that which is deliberately intended to deceive.
media.advanced_definition: Factually erroneous data disseminated irrespective of malicious intent.
media.contextual_example: The rapid spread of medical misinformation on social media undermines public vaccination campaigns.
common_mistakes: 'Disinformation' is deliberately malicious; 'misinformation' can be accidental.

media.definition: The transmission of programmes or information by radio and television.
media.advanced_definition: Electronic distribution of audio and visual signals to broad public audiences.
media.contextual_example: Public service broadcasting is funded by household license fees to ensure political neutrality.
common_mistakes: Past tense of 'broadcast' is usually 'broadcast' (not broadcasted).

media.definition: The presentation of stories in a way that is intended to provoke public interest at the expense of accuracy.
media.advanced_definition: Journalistic exaggeration and emotive distortion engineered to escalate viewership.
media.contextual_example: Tabloid sensationalism undermines serious democratic debate regarding complex economic legislation.

media.definition: The number of copies of a newspaper or magazine that are usually sold each day/week.
media.advanced_definition: Total verified distribution copies of a periodical publication.
media.contextual_example: Print newspaper circulation has plummeted over the past decade as readership transitioned to mobile applications.
common_mistakes: Also means blood flow in medicine.

media.definition: Relating to the commissioning or preparing of material, or expressing author opinion.
media.advanced_definition: Reflecting the authorized institutional opinion of a publication's senior editors.
media.contextual_example: The newspaper published a scathing editorial condemning the municipal government's transit cuts.
common_mistakes: Can be an adjective or a noun.

media.definition: Prejudiced in favor of a particular cause or party.
media.simple_definition: One-sided and biased toward one political party.
media.advanced_definition: Showing blind, uncritical, or aggressive allegiance to a political faction.
media.contextual_example: Cable television news channels have abandoned objective neutrality in favor of hyper-partisan commentary.

academic_english.definition: Provide evidence to support or prove the truth of.
academic_english.advanced_definition: To validate a theoretical claim through corroborating empirical proof.
academic_english.contextual_example: The researcher failed to substantiate his extraordinary thesis with peer-reviewed statistical data.

academic_english.advanced_definition: To render impossible or rule out in advance through prior circumstance.
academic_english.contextual_example: A severe budget deficit does not preclude the municipality from piloting modest cycling corridors.
common_mistakes: Grammar pattern: 'preclude someone FROM doing something'.

academic_english.definition: The process of forming a noun from a verb or adjective; grammatical metaphor.
academic_english.advanced_definition: The syntactic conversion of verbal predicates into nominal abstract entities.
academic_english.contextual_example: Mastering nominalization allows academic writers to compress complex processes into concise topic sentences.

academic_english.definition: Combine two or more texts, ideas, or arguments into one; confuse distinct things.
academic_english.simple_definition: Confuse two different ideas as one.
academic_english.advanced_definition: To fallaciously merge two separate conceptual entities, creating logical error.
academic_english.contextual_example: Public commentary frequently conflates economic growth with equitable human development.

academic_english.definition: Written or spoken communication or debate; a formal discussion of a topic.
academic_english.advanced_definition: Connected speech or writing organized according to institutional norms.
academic_english.contextual_example: Civil public discourse has deteriorated into vitriolic political polarization on social media platforms.
common_mistakes: Stress is on first syllable for noun: /ˈdɪskɔːs/.

academic_english.definition: The combination of ideas to form a theory or system.
academic_english.advanced_definition: The dialectical reconciliation of thesis and antithesis into a higher unified proposition.
academic_english.contextual_example: Her dissertation provides a brilliant synthesis of classical economics and contemporary climate science.

academic_english.definition: A division or contrast between two things that are represented as being opposed or entirely different.
academic_english.advanced_definition: A sharp conceptual bifurcation between two mutually exclusive entities.
academic_english.contextual_example: Educational theorists reject the false dichotomy between vocational apprenticeships and academic scholarship.
common_mistakes: 'False dichotomy' is an essential analytical phrase.

academic_english.advanced_definition: Standing out conspicuously from its context; of paramount significance.
academic_english.contextual_example: The report identifies several salient factors that contributed to the financial crisis.
academic_english.ielts_usefulness: Essential keyword for IELTS Writing Task 1 overviews.
